body:
Yes, I designed the `monitoring_feeds` API based on the macOS backend which is synchronous. It should have been designed with asynchronous use in mind.
It makes sense to me that the boolean flips instantly, but there would be a signal to indicate that feeds are "up-to-date". The name `monitoring_started` sounds good to me. Or perhaps it would be better to have a signal like `feeds_changed`, which updates on every feed change?

body: @shiena I suggest the past tense as other signals: `feeds_updated`

This is not the correct place to emit the signal. The signal should be emitted (probably asynchronously) whenever there are actual updates to the feeds, i.e. from each platform's `CameraServer` subclass respectively.

Since `CameraServer::set_monitoring_feeds(true)` is set after updating camera feeds in each CameraServer subclass, the feeds_updated signal should be emitted properly. Would it be better to explicitly emit the signal in the subclasses?

Not all camera servers have updated the feeds fully when exiting `set_monitoring_feeds`. This is especially the case for Linux — Which is the reason https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/108136 was reported in the first place. The `monitoring_feeds` bool should be `true` immediately after setting `monitoring_feeds = true`, regardless of whether the feeds are already up to date or not.

Additionally, `feeds_updated` should be called whenever there are changes to the current feeds. For example, in `camera_macos`, the appropriate place would be the end of `update_feeds`.

I don't think this is the appropriate place to emit the signal. Feeds are updated both from here and `devices_changed`. Like I said in the other discussion, I think the appropriate place would be the end of `update_feeds`.
Same goes for other platforms.

We use UPPERCASE only for macros. `static` variables should be normal camel_case.

```suggestion
	static constexpr char feeds_updated_signal_name[] = "feeds_updated";
```

This isn't fully thread safe. But I'm noticing on reviewing `SafeFlag` that it's improperly implemented, and cannot be made truly thread safe. For the moment, this is probably fine. I'll address my `SafeFlag` concerns some other time.
I was mistaken. The signal is emitted at the end of `update_feeds`, not after update_feeds.
The call should happen just before `usleep`. Otherwise, it will only be called once we stop monitoring feeds.
Why do the call twice?
Removing this as the fix was missed.
